subject: P1 INFRA: pool slot reclamation is DEAD. /home/eq1/hexworth-sandbox/reclaim-idle-slots.py crashes on import -- it loads '/home/eq1/openstack-stage1/claim_service.py' which does not exist on bc1 (no claim_service.py anywhere on the host, no /home/eq1/openstack* dirs at all). The claim service lives on bc2 per the Stage 3 identity bridge. Nancy separately confirmed the script is in NO crontab on bc1 (checked eq1 and root) -- consistent, since it could not have run anyway. Consequence, in the script's own words: 'Running the gates repeatedly walked the pool to student-30 and exhausted it -- real students would get 503.' Slots bind to a uid PERMANENTLY and nothing releases them. Fix: point it at the bc2 claim service (or run it there), then cron it. Until then every QC gate run permanently consumes a slot from the 40-pool split 28 lab / 12 free-play.
description:
Found 2026-08-01 while cleaning up leaked QC debris
[2026-08-01 01:12] MEASURED + ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-01. The script is simply on the WRONG HOST: claim_service.py lives at /home/eq1/openstack-stage1/claim_service.py on **bc2**, not bc1. Copied it to bc2 and it runs correctly there in report mode. FIX = run it from bc2 (or have the bc1 copy call the bc2 claim service), then cron it. LIVE POOL STATE, read-only: 'pool: 30 slots, 29 bound to a uid, 1 free'. FOUR slots are reclaimable (creds=0 servers=0 volumes=0 -- nothing to lose): student-01, student-04, student-06, student-13. The rest each hold 1 server so the script conservatively keeps them. ONE FREE SLOT means the next student or QC run gets a 503. Running with --apply would take it to 5 free. Not run -- releasing pool bindings is a production state change and the call is not mine to make solo.
[2026-08-01 01:24] NANCY RULING 2026-08-01: PAUSE on --apply as scoped. The resource test (creds=0 servers=0 volumes=0) is NOT sufficient on its own for a real student: IDLE_TIMEOUT is 15 min (server.js:90) and teardown calls deleteBridgeCred(), so creds=0 means 'no container in 15 minutes', not 'no active student'. The capstone's own destroy->rebuild gap is exactly the pause that can exceed 15 min while a student troubleshoots -- so a cron'd reclaim on this test could release a live student's binding mid-lab. My worry was correct and uncovered. STRONGER SIGNAL SHE FOUND: cross-reference bound uids against Firebase Auth. Of the 29 bound slots, 11 resolve to users and ALL 11 are @hexworth-smoke.local QC accounts; the other 18 correspond to NO Firebase user at all (nobody can ever authenticate as them). Zero confirmed real students among the 29. FIX ORDER: layer identity check FIRST (absent from Auth, or matching the QC email pattern = safe regardless of the 15-min collision), and use the resource test as the decider ONLY for uids that are confirmed live non-QC. All 4 named candidates clear on identity. ALSO UNCHECKED: the ~18 identity-dead slots holding servers>0 are invisible to the conservative script, which may mean real hypervisor RAM leaking under identities that can never return for it -- quieter and worse than binding exhaustion.
[2026-08-02 07:48] [2026-08-02] IDENTITY LAYER IS BLOCKED ON CREDENTIALS, not on design. Nancy's fix order needs a Firebase AUTH lookup and no available credential can do one.
- bc2 has NEITHER firebase_admin NOR a service-account key. Adding one puts Firebase creds on a sandbox host = security decision, not mine.
- Local ADC (user creds) gets HTTP 403 from Identity Toolkit: 'application is authenticating by using local Application Default Credentials' -- listUsers and getUser both fail auth/internal-error for ALL 25 uids. A uniform failure across every input is a tool smell, so this was NOT reported as data.
- FIRESTORE fallback works but is a PROXY, not the claim. Result: 0 of 25 bound uids have a users/{uid} doc, absent=25, WITH a control (a known uid resolves exists=true) proving the lookup can succeed. Consistent with Nancy's 'zero confirmed real students' but does NOT prove it -- a real student with no profile doc looks identical to a synthetic uid.
LIVE POOL STATE re-measured read-only from bc2: 30 slots, 25 bound, 5 FREE (was 1 free on 08-01, so something released 4 since).
NOT RUN: --apply. Nancy requires identity-first via Auth and that check does not exist yet.
NEXT STEP IS A DECISION, not code: provision a read-only service account for Auth lookups and decide where it runs (bc2, or a job here that emits a classification the bc2 script consumes). Script is at bc2:/home/eq1/openstack-stage1/reclaim-idle-slots.py (51 lines, no identity check in it today).
[2026-08-02 07:53] [2026-08-02] UPSTREAM CAUSE WAS ALREADY FIXED -- found while reading walkthrough-project.js (_tools/openstack-bridge/, header comment). The gate harnesses USED to mint a random email per run, creating a brand-new Firebase user each time, and the bridge binds a pool slot to a uid PERMANENTLY. That is what walked the pool to exhaustion. They now use a FIXED QC identity (e.g. proj-walk-qc@hexworth-smoke.local), so in the harness's own words QC costs 'a constant 12 slots instead of growing forever'.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TASK: the bleed is STOPPED, and the ~12 QC-bound slots are the bounded steady-state cost of that fix, not a leak. Reclamation is now cleanup of historical debris plus recovering those 12, NOT an ongoing containment need. That lowers the urgency from the original P1 framing -- binding exhaustion is no longer growing. It does NOT lower the urgency of the second problem Nancy named (identity-dead slots holding servers>0 = hypervisor RAM under identities that can never return), which is unaffected by the fixed-identity change.
This also plausibly explains part of the 29-bound -> 25-bound movement between 08-01 and 08-02 without a second actor, though I have NOT confirmed what released those 4 and still consider it unexplained.
[2026-08-02 07:56] [2026-08-02] CREDENTIAL FACT, measured (corrects an assumption in review): NO service-account credential exists on this host. Only ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json with type='authorized_user'; GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS unset; no *-firebase-adminsdk-*.json anywhere under /home/eq. The scripts often cited as proof one exists (audit-xp.js, tenant-admin.js, bulk-unlock.js) make ZERO Auth-admin calls -- authCalls=0, firestoreCalls=2 each. They work because Firestore ACCEPTS user ADC while Identity Toolkit REJECTS it. The scripts that do call Auth admin (index.js, hex-ai-bridge.js, onboarding-state.js) run inside Cloud Functions where the SA is ambient.
LATENT DEFECT IN THE EXISTING TOOL -- functions/audit-pool-slot-owners.js:26 does admin.initializeApp({projectId}) with no credential. Under user ADC every getUser throws a non-user-not-found error, so its own (correct, fail-closed) guard at :38-39 pushes ALL slots into LIVE and it prints 'bound, uid LIVE: 25'. That is SAFE but it is NOT a classification -- it is a uniform-failure artifact wearing a green label, the same shape as the 25x auth/internal-error I refused to report. Anyone running the documented pair today gets an authoritative-looking file that means nothing. Needs an explicit credential-type preflight that ABORTS rather than reporting.
ALSO: the 'free' QC-email-pattern check is NOT free. dump-slot-uids.py emits {slot,project_id,uid} only, and Keystone holds no email -- user student-02 is {id,name:'student-02',domain_id,enabled,default_project_id,password_expires_at,options,links}. Identities are POOL identities; the student address lives only in Firebase Auth. Both halves of the two-part identity test route through the same blocked call. (14 QC addresses, not 12: chain|cinder|net|proj|rescue|sg|wall x adv|walk @hexworth-smoke.local.)
PROPOSED (with Nancy): run the classifier INSIDE a Cloud Function where the Auth SA is already ambient -- no key on bc2, none locally, none newly provisioned. dump-slot-uids.py still runs on bc2 with zero new credentials. Awaiting her ruling.
[2026-08-02 08:00] [2026-08-02] I WAS WRONG: THE BLEED IS NOT STOPPED. Nancy challenged my 'fixed identities => bounded slot cost' claim as repeating a premise BUG-066 already disproved. She was right. Re-measured, and the result confirms BUG-066's mechanism directly.
METHOD (no Auth admin needed, and it discriminates): signInWithPassword with each harness's REAL password from _tools/openstack-bridge/*.js. Success = the account survived and its uid is stable. Never calls signUp, so it cannot create an account or bind a slot. NOTE a wrong-password probe was USELESS -- all 14 returned a uniform INVALID_LOGIN_CREDENTIALS because this project has email-enumeration protection on, which collapses EMAIL_NOT_FOUND into it; a uniform answer across every input is a tool smell and was NOT reported as data. Controls: a definitely-absent address must not sign in (it did not), and real pairs must (5 did).
RESULT: 5 of 14 QC identities survived, 9 could not sign in.
CROSS-CHECK against the 25 bound slots (dump-slot-uids.py output):
  - CURRENT QC identities holding a slot: 2 only -- student-17 <- proj-walk-qc, student-25 <- cinder-adv-qc
  - 23 of 25 bound uids match NO current QC identity
  - 3 surviving QC identities hold no slot yet, so they will bind fresh ones on their next run
That is BUG-066 exactly: the account is purged, recreated with a NEW uid, binds a NEW slot, and the OLD uid stays bound forever. Fixed EMAIL is not fixed UID. So 23 of the 25 bound slots are purge debris and the leak is ONGOING, just slower than the random-email era. Reclamation is active containment after all, not historical cleanup -- my earlier note on this is retracted.
This also removes the need to explain the 29->25 delta as a mystery actor for THAT part of the story, but does NOT explain it: no reclaim ran (bc1 and bc2 both checked -- no crontab entry, no bash_history, script mtimes Jul 31, nothing in openstack-stage1 modified since 08-01). Non-interactive ssh does not write bash_history, so its silence is not evidence either way. The 4 slots that went free are EXACTLY the 4 named reclaimable on 08-01 (student-01/04/06/13, now free along with student-27). Still unexplained and still the most alarming item.
[2026-08-02 08:05] [2026-08-02] (c) /release ESTIMATE, per Nancy's ordering. Read the claim service on bc2.
SHAPE: claim_service.py is a plain BaseHTTPRequestHandler. Existing POST routes: /claim /reconcile /seed /verify /cred (do_POST at :621). Binding is a single Keystone PATCH -- claim() at :162-184 does 'project': {'hexworth_uid': uid}. slot_of(uid) at :553 already implements the exact lookup loop a release needs.
SERVER DIFF: small. release(uid) mirroring slot_of + the inverse PATCH (hexworth_uid: None) is ~15 lines, plus a 3-line 'if self.path == /release' branch in do_POST. Reuses admin_token() and pool_projects(). No new deps, no schema, no migration.
THE CONSTRAINT THAT CHANGES THE DESIGN -- and it rules out the obvious version: /release MUST NOT be called on ordinary session teardown. Sticky mapping is the FEATURE (a returning student gets the same slot and their persisted instances back). Releasing on destroy would unbind real students and their next launch would land on a different slot, orphaning every resource they built -- strictly worse than the leak it fixes. So (c) is NOT 'the bridge releases on teardown'; it is 'the QC HARNESSES release their own slot at end of run'.
CALLER DIFF: ~15 harness scripts in _tools/openstack-bridge/ each need one POST in cleanup, ~3 lines each. e2e-stage3.js (BUG-089) is the one that most needs it since it also mints a random identity.
SAFETY GATE NEEDED ON THE ENDPOINT: it must refuse to release a slot that still holds servers/volumes, or it becomes a way to orphan live resources. That check already exists in reclaim-idle-slots.py's resource test and in /verify -- reuse, do not re-derive.
NET: server ~20 lines + ~45 lines across callers + a resource guard. Cheap. The risk is not the size, it is calling it from the wrong place.
NOT BUILT -- estimate only, per the PAUSE.
[2026-08-02 08:07] [2026-08-02] (c) ESTIMATE REVISED -- Nancy was right that a harness-side /release inherits the process.exit defect. MEASURED which harnesses are affected rather than assuming all of them:
ALREADY FIXED (throw -> finally -> exit, so cleanup runs on failure too): walkthrough-project, adversarial-project, and the chain/neutron/secgroup pairs. walkthrough-project.js:188-198 shows the pattern and the comment states the reason verbatim -- 'fail() throws rather than calling process.exit, because process.exit does not unwind and therefore skipped the session teardown and QC-account deletion on every failing run'.
STILL SKIP CLEANUP (mid-flow 'const fail = ... process.exit(1)'): walkthrough-cinder, walkthrough-rescue, walkthrough-wall, adversarial-cinder, adversarial-rescue, adversarial-wall, e2e-stage3. SEVEN of the fleet.
So a harness-side /release would silently cover only part of the leak, and would look fixed in the walkthrough-passes case while staying broken in exactly the adversarial-fails case those harnesses exist to produce. That is the failure shape Nancy named.
REVISED (c): TWO parts, and the second is not optional.
  1. Apply the throw-then-finally pattern to the 7 stragglers. Mechanical, the correct version already exists in-repo to copy, and BUG-077's record already flagged this class as affecting all six lab harnesses -- so it likely needs doing regardless of /release.
  2. Do NOT let slot return depend on harness cooperation at all. A bridge-side sweep that releases QC-owned slots with no live resources is immune to how any process exits. Harness-side release becomes a fast path, not the guarantee.
This makes (c) bigger than my first estimate (~20 server lines + ~45 caller lines) but it is still small; the cost is in the 7 exit-path edits plus the sweep, not in the endpoint.
STILL NOT BUILT -- estimate only, per the PAUSE.
[2026-08-02 08:09] [2026-08-02] SWEEP DESIGN PINNED -- (A), NOT (B). Written down explicitly because Nancy identified this as the one place the identity gate could be lost by relabeling 'reclaim' as 'sweep'.
(A) IS THE DESIGN: the sweep considers ONLY slots whose bound uid MATCHES an entry on the known, current QC identity list (the 14 fixed @hexworth-smoke.local addresses enumerable from _tools/openstack-bridge/*.js). An unrecognised uid is NEVER touched, by construction. No Auth lookup needed, no ownership inference, and it cannot reach a real student's slot even in principle.
(B) IS REJECTED: running the resource-only test (creds==0 && servers==0 && volumes==0) against ANY bound slot and INFERRING QC ownership. BUG-066 already rejected inferring ownership from resource state or names -- the labs instruct students to create servers with exactly the names the harnesses use, so a name or resource match proves nothing. Adopting (B) under the name 'sweep' would silently drop the identity gate this entire thread exists to enforce.
SCOPE CONSEQUENCE, stated so it is not oversold: (A) only prevents NEW leakage from the 7-straggler class. It does NOTHING for the 23 existing debris slots -- those are by definition bound to uids matching no current identity, so (A) will never touch them. Clearing those remains (d)'s job via Auth-admin getUser -> user-not-found. (c) and (d) are complements, not alternatives; neither substitutes for the other.
RESOURCE TEST STAYS, but DEMOTED: creds/servers/volumes == 0 is an ADDITIONAL guard applied AFTER the identity match, never the decider. It exists to avoid orphaning live resources on a slot we already know is QC-owned.
ACTION LOG IS A PRECONDITION, not a follow-up: the sweep must write (slot, uid, timestamp, reason) durably BEFORE it is ever enabled. BUG-090 is open precisely because a production binding change had no attributable actor; shipping a second automated mutator of the same Keystone property without its own log would compound that forensic gap and make the next investigation have to rule out our own sweep.
7-FILE EXIT FIX IS PER-FILE, NOT PATTERN-STAMPED: the throw-vs-exit SHAPE is common but the cleanup bodies differ by resource type -- cinder pair deletes volumes, wall pair deletes security groups, rescue pair unwinds rescue-mode instances, e2e-stage3 deletes an instance plus the test user. Each gets its own diff verified against its own existing cleanup code.
STILL NOT BUILT.
[2026-08-02 08:17] [2026-08-02] ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED -- THE LEAK IS SELF-INFLICTED, NOT (ONLY) FIREBASE PURGE. Found while fixing exit paths; it also means two commits of mine today briefly made things worse.
MECHANISM, already documented in-repo at adversarial-wall.js:105-111 and missed by me until now: 'Deleting the account frees the email, so the next run signUp mints a NEW uid and binds ANOTHER slot, which is the leak this change exists to stop.' The wall pair ALREADY stopped deleting its QC account for exactly this reason.
13 of 15 harnesses STILL call accounts:delete at the end of every run. So each run destroys its own fixed identity, and the next run creates a new uid that binds a new slot. That is a leak PER RUN PER HARNESS, self-inflicted, and it does not depend on Firebase purging anything.
IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE CENSUS BETTER THAN PURGE DOES: only 5 of 14 QC identities resolved on the sign-in probe. Not because Firebase purged 9 of them -- because their own last run deleted them. And it explains 23 of 25 bound slots being dead uids without needing any purge at all.
MY REGRESSION, corrected in the same session: I moved accounts:delete INTO a finally on walkthrough-cinder and walkthrough-rescue, which made the leak fire on FAILING runs too. Fixed in 45485edbd -- both keep DELETE /destroy in the finally (that session leak was real) and no longer delete the account at all.
RE-SCOPES EVERYTHING: the primary fix is to STOP DELETING THE ACCOUNT in the remaining 11 files (walkthrough-chain/neutron/project/secgroup, adversarial-chain/cinder/neutron/project/rescue/secgroup, e2e-stage3). That is a one-line deletion per file and it stops the leak AT SOURCE. The exit-path work is secondary. (c) the bridge /release becomes much less urgent -- possibly unnecessary for containment -- and (d) is still needed, but only to clear the 23 EXISTING debris slots, not to hold back an ongoing bleed.
BUG-066's stated mechanism is incomplete and should be amended.
[2026-08-02 08:36] [2026-08-02] EXIT-PATH + ACCOUNT-DELETE WORK COMPLETE for 12 of 15 harnesses. Fleet measured: all 15 node --check clean; only e2e-stage3 still exits mid-flow; only walkthrough-project, adversarial-project and e2e-stage3 still delete their account. Those three are exactly Nancy's out-of-scope set. Commits 940c42466, e5e4e177e, 45485edbd, 1aa162a8a, fe7faa1ad. BUG-066 amended with the corrected mechanism.
[2026-08-02 09:42] [2026-08-02] PREFLIGHT MODULE BUILT + PROVEN; wiring the other 13 harnesses is mechanical but currently UNVERIFIABLE.
_tools/openstack-bridge/preflight.js -- findBlockers(dex, slot, names) + report(slot, blockers). Checks (1) INSTANCE QUOTA, which is the UNIVERSAL blocker (--instances 1, and BUG-092 found a stranded server in every one of the 25 bound slots), and (2) per-harness NAME collisions, exact-match. Deletes nothing.
PROVEN: offline two-fixture test (real dirty shape -> 4 blockers, clean -> 0, 'lab-vol-backup' correctly ignored) AND live on student-25, where it reported 4 blockers vs the 3 my inline version caught -- the extra one is the quota, which no name check can see. Wired into adversarial-cinder only.
WHY THE REST ARE NOT WIRED YET: every slot is dirty, so a preflight added to any harness would just report DIRTY TENANT and I could not tell a correct wiring from a broken one. Wiring is safe to finish once the cleanup decision lands.
VERIFIED NAME MAP, read from each harness's own create commands (do NOT guess these):
  chain pair          chain-vm
  walkthrough-cinder  lab-vol, server-a, server-b
  adversarial-cinder  lab-vol, cheat-srv        [DONE]
  neutron pair        lab5-vm  (also creates lab5-net)
  project pair        proj-vm  (also creates proj-net, proj-sg)
  walkthrough-rescue  ghost-srv, rescue-srv
  adversarial-rescue  orphan-vol, ghost-srv, rescue-srv
  walkthrough-wall    wall-vol, phoenix, wall-srv
  adversarial-wall    phoenix
  secgroup pair       guard-vm (also web-sg; adversarial also backdoor-sg)
WIRING RECIPE, two edits per file, require FIRST so there is no invalid intermediate:
  1. after the child_process require:  const preflight = require('./preflight.js');
  2. at the top of the try block:      const stale = preflight.findBlockers(dex, slot, [...names]);
                                       if (stale.length) { preflight.report(slot, stale); fail(...); }
  Both preflight.js AND the harness must be scp'd to ~/hexworth-sandbox -- the require is relative.
KNOWN LIMIT: the preflight scans VOLUMES and SERVERS only. Networks and security groups also persist (BUG-077's analysis turns on exactly that) and are not covered. Worth extending, but the quota check already catches the case that blocks a run.
[2026-08-11 14:27] CLOSED 2026-08-11. The ticket described a broken sweeper; the real finding was that claim_service.py had NO release function at all, so a slot was held for life and 50 slots was a lifetime cap on distinct users. Chain now live and verified end to end: awardCourseBadge (CF, ACTIVE 13:45:45Z) -> bc1 /api/sandbox/release-slot (service key) -> bc2 /release (bridge secret) -> emptiness guard. A REAL student holding 1 server + 2 volumes was targeted through the full chain and correctly REFUSED, binding intact. 4 idle bindings released by hand, 8 bound -> 4, nothing destroyed.

HONEST LIMITS, recorded because they matter more than the fix: it recycles FINISHERS ONLY. A pool fills with people who start and stop; completion never fires for them, and if they left servers running the guard refuses forever. claim() checks RAM (FLOOR_MB) BEFORE slots, so RAM is the binding constraint, not slot count. Measured at close: 4/50 bound, 18.5 GB free. Neither constraint was near binding, so this was architecture on a healthy pool, not an incident, and I measured only after being asked twice whether it was the right fix.

The leak that opened this ticket was ALREADY FIXED before today: all 15 OpenStack harnesses use a fixed QC identity, so QC costs one slot per harness reused forever. I asserted it was still open without checking.

Substrate left behind for any future lifecycle policy: /release endpoint, emptiness guard, bc1 relay, server-issued completion record. Inactivity or instructor-initiated triggers would reuse all three.
